sentinel_issue: The observed room count reached 46,522 on September 11 and remains 46,465 on November 1, roughly nine times the documented 5,120-room cap. This indicates the configured room-count quota is not enforcing the stated bound, leaving namespace squatting and aggregate metadata growth materially less constrained than intended.
worker_response: The apparent violation is an aggregation mismatch: observed capacities are 163,840 or 250,000 rooms (32× or roughly 49× the 5,120 per-namespace cap), so 46,522 rooms is consistent with many namespaces rather than one namespace exceeding its quota. Fix the dashboard and enforcement to report the maximum per-namespace count separately, and add an atomic global room quota if the intended bound is 5,120 across the entire deployment.
auditor_verdict: DISAGREE: the data shows aggregate rooms of 46,522 versus 5,120, while capacities of 163,840 and 250,000 are 32× and 48.8× the cap, but it provides no per-namespace counts or namespace identities. Thus aggregation mismatch is plausible, not demonstrated; separate per-namespace reporting and an atomic global quota are appropriate fixes if 5,120 is intended deployment-wide.
